facts.text: The clone is a Python library for the Newport SMC100 motor controller
The class smc100 talks to an SMC100 through a serial port
The constructor opens the serial port at 57600 baud with 8 data bits, no parity, one stop bit and a 10 s timeout
A command is sent as the command text plus CRLF; a query returns the reply with the first len(command) characters removed
The controller state is queried with '%02dTS' and the last two characters of the reply are looked up in controller_state_map
controller_state_map names MOVING, READY from MOVING and DISABLE from READY
get_position queries '%02dTP' and its docstring says the value is in mm, but the parsed value is printed and the method returns None
get_errors queries '%02dTS', maps the error bits through error_names and returns [None] when there is no error
set_velocity writes '%02dVA%f' and get_velocity queries '%02dVA?', but the parsed velocity is printed and get_velocity returns None
home writes '%02dOR'; home_until_done polls get_state with a 0.5 s sleep in an unbounded loop
The constructor sets motors_count to 1 and reads info for one controller
When the serial open fails the constructor prints that it uses a dummy motor controller but does not replace the serial object
The README calls the controller argument the motor number, usually 1
The README describes the move position as between 0-27 without a unit
The README links an external SMC100CC/SMC100PP user manual and says to refer to it

operator_required.name: velocity
operator_required.reason: no text file of the clone states the velocity range or its unit; the site sets the native velocity range

operator_required.name: move_absolute
operator_required.reason: no text file of the clone states the travel of the configured stage; the README's 0-27 for the move position (README.md:28) has no unit and is the library author's example, so the site sets the absolute position range

operator_required.name: move_relative
operator_required.reason: a relative move can be positive or negative and no text file of the clone states a step or travel bound; the site sets the relative move range
